interest: Reveals debates over taxing foreign nationals, early Shoup Mission proposals, and legal limits on pre-peace treaty tax conventions.
keywords: American Chamber of Commerce in Japan
overview: This file documents United States and Allied policy regarding taxation in occupied Japan between 1946 and 1949 under the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP). It encompasses Far Eastern Commission consultations on Japanese extraordinary taxation and Allied safeguards, State Department legal evaluations concerning the feasibility of negotiating a bilateral double taxation convention before a peace treaty, and preliminary reform recommendations from the Shoup Tax Mission. It also includes appeals against excessive reassessments and joint proposals from Allied trade bodies advocating tax deductions for foreign businessmen to support economic recovery.
